sources.entry: VimR - Refined Neovim experience for macOS.

summary.one_liner: VimR is a Neovim GUI application for macOS, written in Swift, that embeds Neovim with additional graphical editor features.
summary.what_it_does: VimR wraps Neovim in a native macOS window and adds GUI conveniences similar to other editors. The README lists features including a Markdown preview, a generic HTML preview that keeps scroll position on reload, a fuzzy file finder modeled on Xcode's "Open Quickly", and trackpad pinch-to-zoom and two-finger scrolling. It also offers optional ligatures (off by default), a command line tool, a simple file browser, and a flexible workspace model similar to JetBrains IDEs. The project is modular, and several Swift packages (NvimView, NvimApi, Commons, Tabs, Workspace, Ignore) are described as usable independently.
use_cases: edit code in a native macOS Neovim window
quickly open files by fuzzy name search
embed Neovim in a Cocoa app via NvimView
use Neovim with trackpad gestures and GUI tabs
notable: Embeds the Neovim binary and runtime files via the NvimView SwiftPM module
Built on a Redux-style architecture, per the README
Markdown and generic HTML preview inside the editor
Modular Swift packages usable independently (NvimApi, Commons, Tabs, Workspace, Ignore)
caveats: Requires macOS 13.0 or later and Xcode 26 for development
Pre-built binaries are provided under Releases; building from source requires Homebrew and submodule setup
Ad-hoc signing is used when notarize=false is set
